records.issue_text: When all email rows are removed, `handleAdd` in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:49-51 returns silently with no user feedback — the Add button appears to do nothing
records.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, `handleAdd` returns early when `multiEmailValue.length === 0` (lines ~49-51) with no toast/error state update. The `MultiEmail` component allows removing rows via `updatedValue.splice(index, 1)`; removing the last row can set the value to `[]`. In that state, clicking the Add button results in a silent no-op, matching the finding.

records.issue_text: The `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43-44 is dead code because the template string is always non-empty, exposing raw output like `BAD_REQUEST: emails_must_be_unique_valid` to users
records.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx onError, `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` always produces a non-empty string (even if `err.data?.code` is undefined it becomes `'undefined: ...'`), so `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), ...)` will never use the fallback. This can surface raw codes/keys like `BAD_REQUEST: emails_must_be_unique_valid` to end users, as the finding states.

records.issue_text: `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` at addGuests.handler.ts:169-171 discards the error, making email delivery failures undiagnosable in production
records.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the new `try/catch` around `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` catches any error but only logs a generic message (`console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")`) and does not include `err` or rethrow. This is verifiable from the diff and creates an observability/diagnostics gap for production email delivery failures, even if core booking updates still succeed.
